# Cancer Distribution

This folder contains topics related to specific medical conditions and epidemiological distributions observed in acute surgical patients within the Danish healthcare system. It includes a detailed breakdown of cancer prevalence among acute surgery patients nationally and across the Capital Region, alongside clinical data on perforated ulcers, highlighting the critical impact of surgical delays on patient survival and historical decisions regarding national monitoring.

## Pages

- [[cancer-distribution|Cancer Distribution]] — Details the prevalence of gastrointestinal, gynecological, and other cancers among acute surgical patients nationally and across hospitals in the Capital Region.
- [[perforeret-ulcus|perforeret ulcus]] — Documents the clinical condition of perforated ulcers, emphasizing the 2.4% hourly decrease in survival probability with surgical delays and the 2018 decision to halt national monitoring of bleeding ulcers.
